The '''2021–22 Liga Portugal''' (also known as '''Liga Portugal Bwin'''<ref>{{cite web|date=16 April 2021|url=https://www.ligaportugal.pt/pt/epocas/20202021/noticias/institucional/liga-portugal-e-bwin-formalizam-acordo-de-parceria-para-as-proximas-5-temporadas/|title=Liga Portugal and Bwin establish a partnership agreement for the next 5 seasons|language=en|website=[[Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional|Liga Portugal]]|access-date=20 May 2021|archive-date=21 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210621232858/https://www.ligaportugal.pt/pt/epocas/20202021/noticias/institucional/liga-portugal-e-bwin-formalizam-acordo-de-parceria-para-as-proximas-5-temporadas/|url-status=dead}}</ref> for sponsorship reasons) was the 88th season of the [[Primeira Liga]], the top professional league for Portuguese [[association football]] clubs, and the first season under the current [[Primeira Liga|Liga Portugal]] Bwin title. This was the fifth Primeira Liga season to use video assistant referee (VAR). The start and end dates for the season were released on 21 May 2021,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.jn.pt/desporto/conheca-o-calendario-da-25-a-33-jornada-da-liga-12228661.html|title=Conheça o calendário da 25.ª à 33.ª jornada da Liga|date=22 May 2021|work=Jornal de Noticías|access-date=31 October 2021}}</ref> and the fixtures were released on 8 July 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ojogo.pt/futebol/noticias/kick-off-202122-os-premios-oficiais-e-o-sorteio-dos-campeonatos-ao-minuto-13918176.html|title=Kick-Off 2021/22: os premiados, as declarações e o sorteio dos calendários|website=O Jogo|access-date=2021-07-08}}</ref>

[[Sporting CP]] were the defending champions, having won their nineteenth Primeira Liga and their first title since the [[2001–02 Primeira Liga|2001–02 season]] at the previous season. [[G.D. Estoril Praia|Estoril]], [[FC Vizela|Vizela]] and [[F.C. Arouca|Arouca]] joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2020–21 Liga Portugal 2]]. They replaced [[S.C. Farense|Farense]], [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]] and [[Rio Ave F.C.|Rio Ave]], which were relegated to Liga Portugal 2 the [[2020–21 Liga Portugal 2|previous season]].

This season saw the return of full capacity crowds, after the final third of the [[2019–20 Primeira Liga|2019–20]] and the entirety of the [[2020–21 Primeira Liga|2020–21]] seasons were held with limited or no attendance due to the restrictions caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/desporto/adeptos-regressam-aos-estadios-liga-portugal-garante-seguranca_v1339208|title=Adeptos regressam aos estádios. Liga Portugal garante segurança|first=Rádio e Televisão de|last=Portugal|website=Adeptos regressam aos estádios. Liga Portugal garante segurança}}</ref>

[[FC Porto|Porto]] secured their 30th league title with one match remaining, following a 1–0 away victory over [[O Clássico|rivals]] [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] on 7 May 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abola.pt/nnh/2022-05-07/liga-fc-porto-sagra-se-campeao-na-luz/https%3a%2f%2fwww.abola.pt%2fnnh%2f2022-05-07%2fliga-fc-porto-sagra-se-campeao-na-luz%2f940002|title=FC Porto sagra-se campeão nacional (Liga)|website=A Bola|language=Portuguese|accessdate=11 July 2024|archive-date=23 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220523232443/https://www.abola.pt/nnh/2022-05-07/liga-fc-porto-sagra-se-campeao-na-luz/https:%2F%2Fwww.abola.pt%2Fnnh%2F2022-05-07%2Fliga-fc-porto-sagra-se-campeao-na-luz%2F940002|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Teams==
Eighteen teams compete in the league – the top fifteen teams from [[2020–21 Primeira Liga|the previous season]] and three teams promoted from the [[2020–21 LigaPro|LigaPro]]: [[G.D. Estoril Praia|Estoril]],<ref>{{cite web|date=9 May 2021|url=https://www.ligaportugal.pt/pt/epocas/20202021/noticias/geral/liga-portugal-sabseg/jornada-32/estoril-praia-e-o-novo-campeao-da-liga-portugal-sabseg/|title=Estoril Praia are the new Champions of the Liga Portugal SABSEG|language=en|website=[[Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional|Liga Portugal]]|access-date=6 May 2020}}</ref> [[FC Vizela|Vizela]]<ref>{{cite web|date=22 May 2021|url=https://www.ligaportugal.pt/en/epocas/20202021/noticias/geral/liga-portugal-sabseg/jornada-34/fc-vizela-vence-e-garante-subida-a-liga-nos?bck=L2VuL2hvbWVwYWdlLw|title=FC Vizela win and get promoted to the Liga NOS|language=en|website=[[Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional|Liga Portugal]]|access-date=23 May 2020|archive-date=23 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210523005140/https://www.ligaportugal.pt/en/epocas/20202021/noticias/geral/liga-portugal-sabseg/jornada-34/fc-vizela-vence-e-garante-subida-a-liga-nos?bck=L2VuL2hvbWVwYWdlLw|url-status=dead}}</ref> and [[F.C. Arouca|Arouca]].<ref>{{cite web|date=22 May 2021|url=https://www.ligaportugal.pt/pt/epocas/20202021/noticias/geral/playoff/fc-arouca-na-liga-nos?bck=L3B0L2hvbWVwYWdlLw|title=FC Arouca promoted to Liga NOS|language=en|website=[[Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional|Liga Portugal]]|access-date=23 May 2020}}</ref>

===Changes===
[[G.D. Estoril Praia|Estoril]] (promoted after a three-year absence) and [[FC Vizela|Vizela]] (promoted after a 36-year absence) were promoted from the [[2020–21 Liga Portugal 2]] (finishing 1st and 2nd places), replacing [[S.C. Farense|Farense]] and [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]] (both relegated after only one year in the top flight).

[[F.C. Arouca|Arouca]] (promoted after a four-year absence) was promoted after finishing in 3rd place in [[2020–21 Liga Portugal 2]] and winning the [[#Relegation play-offs|Promotion play-offs]] against [[Rio Ave F.C.|Rio Ave]] (relegated after thirteen years in the top flight).

==Relegation play-offs==
The relegation play-offs took place on 21 and 29 May 2022 between Moreirense who finished 16th in the Primeira Liga and Chaves who finished 3rd in [[2021–22 Liga Portugal 2|Liga Portugal 2]].
